_doc: Walks to a goal (generated by tools/trails/goal_walks.py from OpenStreetMap, ODbL, and the Copernicus DEM; never edit by hand).

trails.name: Kerling summit
trails.why: Mount Kerling is the highest mountain in the District of Eyjafjarðarsveit, in the northern part of Iceland.

trails.name: Hekla summit
trails.why: Hekla is a 1,491 m volcano in the south of Iceland.

trails.name: Ok summit
trails.why: Ok is a shield volcano in Iceland, to the west of Langjökull. It erupted during interglacials in the Pleistocene.

trails.name: Esja summit
trails.why: Esja, more commonly called Esjan, is a 914 m mountain situated in the south-west of Iceland, about 10 km to the north of Iceland's capital city Reykjavík.Esja is not a single mountain, but a volcanic mountain range, made from basalt and tuff.

trails.name: Hvalfell
trails.why: Hvalfell is a table mountain of palagonite at the head of Botnsdalur, in Hvalfjörður.

trails.name: Útigönguhöfði summit
trails.why: Útigönguhöfði is an 805 m mountain above Básar in Goðaland, with paths on both sides.

trails.name: Hengill summit
trails.why: Hengill volcano is situated in the southwest of Iceland, to the south of Þingvellir.

trails.name: Hafnarfjall
trails.why: Hafnarfjall is an 844 m mountain 4 km south-east of Borgarnes, named in the Book of Settlements.

trails.name: Þríhyrningur summit
trails.why: Þríhyrningur is a palagonite mountain near Hvolsvöllur, seen from all over the southern lowlands.

trails.name: Strákar summit
trails.why: Strákar is a mountain at the tip of Tröllaskagi, between Úlfsdalir and Siglufjörður, named after the rock pinnacles on its northern end.

trails.name: Búrfell
trails.why: Búrfell in Grímsnes is a 534 m palagonite mountain just east of Úlfljótsvatn.

trails.name: mountain in southwestern Iceland summit
trails.why: Álútur is a mountain in south-west Iceland, about 6 km north of Hveragerði.

trails.name: Hafragilsfoss
trails.why: Hafragilsfoss is a waterfall in Iceland. The waterfall flows downstream from Dettifoss within the depths of the Jökulságljúfur canyon.

trails.name: Granni waterfall
trails.why: The Granni is a waterfall that cascades into the Þjórsá valley right beside the Háifoss. These two waterfalls did not have a name until the beginning of the 19th century, but Nágranni or granni is the Icelandic word for neighbor while Hái means tall.
